pr_title: swaybar: use text subpixel antialias only where it would look good
pr_body:
Closes #5605

Text Subpixel antialiasing is :

- FreeType makes glyph bitmaps containing coverage percentage for each
  subpixel, instead of pixel
- Then draw by performing the blend for each subpixel, instead of pixel (e.g.
  dual-source blending in opengl)

And there's only one Alpha channel, so this extra coverage data can't
leave Cairo to reach the compositor through there.
Therefore, it can't work as intended if output text alpha != bar background
alpha. Disable it for those cases, enable it elsewhere

As for color emojis, they are RGBA bitmaps. If drawn with text alpha=1.0
and background alpha=1.0 (should be completely opaque bar), then with
'CAIRO_OPERATOR_SOURCE' texels with alpha < 1.0 result in a blend with
whatever's behind the bar, instead of the bar background
pr_comments:
I would rather have 'OVER' for everything, but it would ruin it for setups setting all colors with a same <1 opacity, to produce the same result as an opaque bar drawn whole with that opacity value.
And that's the normal way to get a translucent bar, right ?

issue_context.title: swaybar/swaynag: no subpixel text antialiasing
comments: Can you open an issue on the Cairo bug tracker?

I wanted to, but after preparing the repro, and especially after reading the history of this same problem for i3 (https://github.com/i3/i3/pull/3947. I should have started there, duh), I now think what cairo's doing is not unreasonable, and that a corresponding fix would end up not being used :

- the triple-rate blending for 'source' is only skipped for targets that write an alpha channel (need the grayscale glyphs for that)
- the invoked use case for i3's use of 'source' is to draw an opaque bar, then carve the text back through it with a font color alpha=0. In this case (and in fact any other relying on the compositor to materialize the text from the alpha), subpixel antialiasing musn't be used in the first place
- with 'source', it is not possible to draw a completely opaque bar if it contains color emoji

So there wouldn't be a middle ground between disallowing subpixel AA and changing the operator ?
Hmm, I don't understand a lot of this. Feel free to open a PR if it fixes a bug, please write an explanation in the commit message :P
